h1: Guinea-Bissau tourist visa from the UK
intro: Planning a holiday or a visit to family or friends in Guinea-Bissau? This page explains the Guinea-Bissau tourist visa, who needs one and what to prepare. We check the rules for your passport and apply for you.
eligibility: You are travelling for a holiday, sightseeing or to visit family or friends
You won’t work or do business during your visit
You have a return ticket and enough money for your stay

sections.heading: Do you need a Guinea-Bissau tourist visa?
sections.text: British passport holders need a visa to visit Guinea-Bissau, applied for before you travel.

sections.heading: What a Guinea-Bissau tourist visa covers
sections.text: A Guinea-Bissau tourist visa is for holidays, sightseeing and visiting family or friends in Guinea-Bissau. It doesn't cover business meetings or paid work. If you're travelling for business, see our [Guinea-Bissau business visa](/guinea-bissau-business-visa-uk/) page.

sections.heading: UK residents on other passports
sections.text: UK residents on other passports also need to apply in advance. The process has changed several times, so we confirm the current route for your trip before applying.

sections.heading: Guinea-Bissau tourist visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and handle Guinea-Bissau tourist visa applications for travellers across the UK, entirely online. Before you travel, read the UK government's [foreign travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice) for Guinea-Bissau.

sections.heading: Before you travel to Guinea-Bissau
sections.text:
Check the UK government’s [travel advice for Guinea-Bissau](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/guinea-bissau) before you book, and again shortly before you go. It covers safety, local laws, health risks and the latest entry rules.

- Passport: most countries expect it to be valid for at least six months after you arrive, with blank pages for stamps. If yours is close to expiry, renew it first.
- Health: check the NHS fitfortravel website for Guinea-Bissau at least eight weeks before you travel, in case you need vaccinations or malaria tablets. Some countries ask for a yellow fever certificate if you’ve recently been somewhere with yellow fever.
- Insurance: take out travel insurance that covers medical treatment and getting you home, and check it’s valid for Guinea-Bissau.
- Bookings: carry copies of your return ticket and accommodation, as border officers can ask to see them.

We go through the entry requirements for your passport when we prepare your application, so you know exactly what to carry.

faqs.q: Can I visit family on a Guinea-Bissau tourist visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Visiting family or friends is covered by the Guinea-Bissau tourist visa.

faqs.q: Can I work in Guinea-Bissau on a Guinea-Bissau tourist visa?
faqs.a: No. Working needs a work visa or permit. Contact us and we’ll explain the options.

faqs.q: How long does a Guinea-Bissau tourist visa take?
faqs.a: Usually a few working days, but processing times vary. Apply at least a week before you travel, and earlier in busy seasons.

faqs.q: Do I need travel insurance for Guinea-Bissau?
faqs.a: We strongly recommend it. Choose a policy that covers medical treatment and repatriation, and check it’s valid for your destination before you go.
